animal noun

also animals, creature, beast

classical

Cic. ND 2.122
Plin. NH 9.42
Traupman 141
M-O s.v. animal

animal, animālis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

animal, living creature

Any living creature, man included (animal … homō, Cic. Leg. 1.22), but as often the beasts as against man (Lewis & Short). An i-stem: ablative animālī, plural animālia, animālium.

Other words

  • 1bēstia: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 71, s.v. bēstia; the series spelling of the libellī.

    bēstia1, bēstiae f. — beast, any creature but man

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 81: in bēstiīs, volucribus, nantibus, agrestibus, cicuribus, ferīs; M-O s.v. animal · Declension on Wiktionary

    Cicero’s word for every creature but man, tame or wild (Lewis & Short); also the wild beast of the arena. Its diminutive bēstiola is a little creature, a bug (Cic. ND 2.123).

  • fera, ferae f. — wild animal

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 138: Quās ferās ibi vīdistī?; Phaedr. 1 prol. 5–7: quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae · Declension on Wiktionary

    The wild animal, the talking beast of the fables; properly the feminine of ferus, wild.

Examples

  • alia animālia gradiendō, alia serpendō ad pāstum accēdunt, alia volandō, alia nandō

    some animals come to their food walking, some crawling, some flying, some swimmingCic. ND 2.122

  • nūllum animal graviōre somnō premitur

    no animal sleeps more soundly (of the seal)Plin. NH 9.42

  • Aperīs tū manum tuam, et implēs omne animal benedictiōne.

    You open your hand and fill every living thing with blessing (the grace before meals).Vulg. Ps. 144 (145), 16

  • Quod animal tē potissimum dēlectāvit?

    Which animal did you like best?Traupman 138

See also pet, zoo, livestock, feed, stuffed animal.
